title: GitHub CI Overview
description: CI health, issues, and pull requests across the sdr-enthusiasts and fredsystems organisations. Sourced from github-ci-exporter on sdrhub.

panels.title: Failing Workflows
panels.description: Workflows whose latest default-branch run failed. Excludes cancelled, skipped, and runs aged out past 90 days.

panels.title: Passing Workflows
panels.description: Workflows whose latest default-branch run succeeded.

panels.title: Repos Monitored
panels.description: Non-archived repositories with at least one workflow file.

panels.title: Auto-Disabled
panels.description: Workflows GitHub disabled after 60 days of repository inactivity. These have stopped running silently.

panels.title: Failing Workflows (default branch)
panels.description: Latest branch-state run per workflow that failed. Pull-request runs are excluded: the API's branch filter matches a PR's head branch, so a merged PR's pre-merge failure would otherwise appear here forever.

panels.title: PRs Failing Checks
panels.description: Open non-draft PRs whose head-commit checks failed. These are broken and need fixing.

panels.title: Green, Awaiting Merge
panels.description: Checks pass and the branch is mergeable, but auto-merge is not armed. These are waiting on a human to press the button.

panels.title: Conflicting
panels.description: Open non-draft PRs that conflict with the base branch and need a rebase.

panels.title: Total Needing Action
panels.description: Open non-draft PRs that are failing, conflicting, or ready to merge without auto-merge.

panels.title: Broken Pull Requests
panels.description: Open non-draft PRs whose checks failed, or which conflict with the base branch. Bot-authored PRs are included: a renovate PR failing CI is exactly as actionable as a human one, and often more so because it blocks a dependency bump.

panels.title: Green and Waiting on a Merge
panels.description: Checks pass, no conflicts, and auto-merge is NOT armed, so nothing will land these without a click. This is the state renovate PRs sit in on repositories where platformAutomerge is disabled.

panels.title: Auto-Disabled and Stale Workflows
panels.description: Two different things, so read the Reason column. auto-disabled means GitHub switched the workflow off after 60 days of repository inactivity: it has silently stopped running and is a fault. 'no recent run' means the newest run against the default branch is over 90 days old, which is only a fault for a workflow that has a cadence -- on push or on schedule. A workflow driven by workflow_dispatch or repository_dispatch appears here simply because nothing has asked it to run lately, and a workflow that only runs on pull_request has no default-branch state at all; its failures belong in the pull request panels above. Neither reason means the workflow is failing.

panels.title: Failing Workflows Over Time
panels.description: Trend in failing workflows. A step change usually means one shared action broke across many repositories rather than several independent regressions.

panels.title: Open Issues (human)
panels.description: Issues opened by people. Bot-filed issues are counted separately.

panels.title: Open Issues (bot)
panels.description: Issues filed by renovate, dependabot, and other GitHub Apps. Classified via GraphQL __typename rather than a login list.

panels.title: Open PRs (human)
panels.description: Pull requests opened by people, drafts included.

panels.title: Open PRs (bot)
panels.description: Automated dependency and flake-update pull requests.

panels.title: Open Human Issues by Repository
panels.description: Repositories with issues opened by people, excluding bot-filed noise.

panels.title: Oldest Open Human Pull Requests
panels.description: Non-draft pull requests by people, oldest first. Bot PRs are excluded: renovate holds PRs open by design.

panels.title: Exporter Up
panels.description: Whether Prometheus can reach the exporter. If this is down, every panel above is stale.

panels.title: Last Collection
panels.description: Time since the last successful collection cycle.

panels.title: Core Budget
panels.description: Remaining REST API requests. Independent of the GraphQL pool.

panels.title: GraphQL Budget
panels.description: Remaining GraphQL points. Separate 5000/hour allowance from core.

panels.title: API Rate-Limit Budget
panels.description: Remaining budget per pool. core and graphql are independent 5000/hour allowances, so a healthy graphql figure does not imply a healthy core one.

panels.title: Requests vs Cache Hits
panels.description: Conditional requests answered 304 Not Modified are not charged against the rate limit. In steady state almost every request should be a cache hit; a persistent gap means the ETag cache is not working.

panels.title: Repos Skipped
panels.description: Repositories excluded from monitoring, by reason. Explains an unexpectedly small dashboard without reading exporter logs.

panels.title: Collection Duration
panels.description: Time taken by the last collection cycle.

panels.title: Cycles Bypassed
panels.description: Cycles skipped entirely because the remaining API budget could not cover a full sweep.
